q: How do I count emissions from refining crude glycerine?
title: Refining crude glycerine: emissions
short: Refining crude glycerine is mostly vacuum distillation and bleaching, so steam and electricity are your own emissions. The crude glycerine is a by-product of biodiesel or soap, and how much of that process it carries depends on the allocation rule you choose.
audience: Glycerine refiners and pharma or cosmetics buyers

ul: Steam for distillation, from boiler fuel.
Activated carbon and chemicals, in Scope 3.

p: Ask the supplier how the crude was allocated. A mass basis gives glycerine more burden than an economic basis.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
